theme: Joining stories: push them together and count

activities.title: Push them together
activities.intro: Some here, and some there. When we push them together we get one big lot, and then we can count it. Listen to the story, touch each one as you count, then tap how many there are altogether.
activities.offScreen: Put two toys in one hand and three toys in the other, push your hands together, and count them all for a grown-up.

rounds.prompt: Two red birds were here and three blue birds were there. Now they are all on one branch together. Tap how many birds there are altogether.
Three green leaves were on this side and three yellow leaves were on that side. Now they are in one pile together. Tap how many leaves there are altogether.
Four brown blocks were in the box and one red block was on the floor. Now they are all in one tower together. Tap how many blocks there are altogether.
One big fish was in the pond and three little fish swam over from the stream. Now they are all swimming together. Tap how many fish there are altogether.

activities.title: Where did they come from
activities.intro: These got pushed together and now they are all mixed up. Put them back into the two piles they came from. Then count one pile, count the other pile, and count them all together.
activities.offScreen: Mix up your blocks and your toy animals in one pile, then put them back into two piles and count each one out loud.

rounds.prompt: The red flowers came from the garden and the yellow flowers came from the pot. Put them back into two piles, then count each pile and then count them all together.
The stones came from the path and the coins came from the purse. Put them back into two piles, then count each pile and then count them all together.
The little fish came from the stream and the big fish came from the pond. Put them back into two piles, then count each pile and then count them all together.
The brown blocks came from the shelf and the red blocks came from the basket. Put them back into two piles, then count each pile and then count them all together.

activities.title: Some more came along
activities.intro: In these stories some were already there, and then some more came along and joined them. The ones that came along are a different colour, so you can see who is new. Tap how many there are now.
activities.offScreen: Line up three toys, then bring one more toy over to join them, and tell a grown-up how many there are now.

rounds.prompt: Three blue birds were already on the branch. One red bird flew over and joined them. Tap how many birds are on the branch now.
Four green leaves were already on the twig. Two yellow leaves floated down and joined them. Tap how many leaves are on the twig now.
Two grey stones were already on the path. Three brown stones rolled down and joined them. Tap how many stones are on the path now.
One purple cup was already on the table. Three green cups came from the shelf and joined it. Tap how many cups are on the table now.

parentCard.title: The counting book, one page at a time
steps: Pick a counting storybook together, one with things to count on the pages. Sit so they can see the pictures and you can see their hands.
Read a page aloud, then stop before you turn it. Ask them to put up one finger for every thing on the page, touching each picture as they count out loud.

Find a page with things in two places, some here and some there. Count the first lot onto one hand, count the second lot onto the other hand, then push the two hands together and ask how many altogether.
Ask how many altogether every single time, and then wait, even when the waiting feels long. If they stall, count the first lot for them and let them carry on from there.
Close the book at the end and ask them to make up one joining story of their own on their fingers, about anything they like.
notice: When the two hands come together, do they go back to one and start again, or do they carry on counting from the number in the first hand?
Do they touch each thing as they say its number, or does their voice run ahead of their finger?
Which page did they want to go back to?
